title: The Way Through
human_question: Is there a way through suffering, and what would it take to walk it?
journey: Chathura meets people who have set something down: meditators, pilgrims, forest hermitages, ordinary people who let go. The group ends where the chronology meets the crowd and Chathura turns toward the road.
surface: Stillness, clarity, and the courage of letting go.
depth: The path has two wings, calm (samatha) and insight (vipassanā). Meditation subjects, jhāna and the absorption process; the thirty-seven requisites; the seven purifications as a map from conduct to knowledge; the noble persons; path and fruition. Nibbāna, the one unconditioned reality, completes the four ultimates first named in Group 1.

arc.middle: Calm, then insight: purification, path and release, seen through people who practise.
arc.closing: The final development film ends in the crowd, which is Episode 1's opening image. Released as Episode 99, it hands directly to Episode 100.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The last stage asks whether there is a way through suffering. The texts describe two wings, settling the mind and seeing clearly, walked in order from honest living to understanding, and they separate holding a problem down from cutting it at the root. At the end they name a peace that is not a feeling or a place, and not built but uncovered.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අවසාන අදියර අසන්නේ දුකින් එතෙර වීමට මගක් තිබේද යන්නයි. ග්‍රන්ථ එම මග සිත සන්සුන් කිරීම හා පැහැදිලිව දැකීම යන පියාපත් දෙකෙන්, හොඳ හැසිරීමේ සිට අවබෝධය දක්වා පිළිවෙළින් යන මගක් ලෙසත්, එහි අවසානය හැඟීමක් හෝ ස්ථානයක් නොවන නිවන ලෙසත් දක්වයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma texts describe a path with two kinds of work: calm (samatha), trained on one of forty meditation subjects matched to the person, and insight (vipassanā), which alone brings the path. They map it as seven purifications, from conduct and a settled mind through to knowledge and vision, and describe absorption as deepening by letting go of coarser factors, with mastery meaning the ability to enter, stay, leave and review at will. At the path moment calm and insight pull together, and what is cut off there does not return, unlike tendencies that are only held down. The journey closes on Nibbāna, the fourth ultimate reality, taught as unconditioned, realised rather than produced, and neither a feeling nor a place.
progression: EPD-0087 The Last Instalment: release is a different good from pleasure, and people value it above almost anything.
EPD-0088 Forty Doors: the path starts from many doors, each matched to a person, and settling the mind serves clear seeing.
EPD-0089 Held, Not Touched: attention held long on one object grips it instead of brushing it, and grows simpler as it deepens.
EPD-0090 Thinner Every Time: each stage is mastered before it looks coarse, and deeper means letting go, not adding.
EPD-0091 Reading the Field: practical wisdom sees growth, decline and the right move, and rests on conduct and a steady mind.
EPD-0092 The Crossing: letting go and standing firm are two different moments in the texts' account of the path.
EPD-0093 The Same Crossing: the same arrival can be reached from different depths of calm, and the road colours it.
EPD-0094 Cutting It Out: holding a tendency down is not the same as cutting it at the root so it cannot return.
EPD-0095 What No Longer Comes Up: suppression, temporary displacement and uprooting are three different kinds of change.
EPD-0096 The Rarest Readiness: extraordinary abilities, as the texts describe them, rest on patient training, and instant calm readiness to help is ranked rarest.
EPD-0097 Before the Long Trip: even the deepest withdrawal the texts describe is entered responsibly, with duties to others and a fixed return.
EPD-0098 The Emptied Room: Nibbāna, the fourth ultimate reality, is taught as unconditioned, not a feeling or a place, and uncovered rather than built.
lesson.builds_on: Group 9 showed that what arises by conditions can also cease by conditions, so there is a way through; Group 10 takes up that promise and follows the texts along the way itself, from settling the mind to cutting a tendency at its root, and completes the map of four ultimate realities first named in Group 1.
lesson.hands_to_next: It hands directly to Episode 100, "The Way Back": the last film ends in the crowd that opens Episode 1, and the finale follows Chathura back along the road to the forest, leaving open on screen the question this group raised, what it would take to walk the way through.
